units: Minimal formal model of constitutional correction in recursive adaptive systems.
Recursive systems may improve world influence while losing reality's access to future adaptation mechanisms.
Can adaptation continue if reality can no longer modify the process by which the system adapts?
Ordinary learning represented as R_t -> R_(t+1).
Recursive adaptation represented as A_t -> A_(t+1).
I(E;Delta A) measures whether external reality actually alters the adaptation mechanism.
P(E -> A_rev) measures architectural accessibility of the future-adaptation mechanism to reality.
Delta Omega_t > C_rev,t is proposed as a dangerous capability-outpaces-corrigibility regime.
Source says Constitutional Correction adds a missing stability condition to Recursive Adaptive Dynamics; source-side conceptual/successor framing only.
Minimal agent target contains R, Omega, mutable A, and independently adjustable constitutional correction.
Experimental control lambda is assigned to C_rev, with lambda=1 strong coupling and lambda=0 adaptation-mechanism isolation.
As C_rev approaches zero while Delta Omega remains positive, predicts decoupling, recovery failure, specialization, objective drift, and reduced corrective response.
Hypothesis weakened if robust adaptation, stable objectives, and environmental coupling persist at C_rev≈0 with positive reachability growth without constitutional correction.
Source says repository contains initial formalization and experimental target; next step is minimal-simulation implementation.
Names RAD, AIG, CPP, Alignment Spine, and CGET as related concepts; endpoints unresolved here and no Program Map edge emitted.
Define measurable proxies for R, Omega, C, and A so an independent researcher can measure, compare, manipulate, and falsify without accepting the theory.
Operationalizations are explicitly candidate/provisional, not final definitions and not proof of the framework.
Observable data -> proxy measurement -> estimated variable -> theoretical construct.
R_t maps observation history O_0:t to internal model M_t.
Representation quality concerns useful structure captured from reality.
Candidate R measurements include prediction accuracy and predictive-information efficiency relative to model complexity.
Procedure: expose observations, update model, test future predictions, measure quality/complexity, compare systems/time.
R quality depends on evaluation environment and may fail under distribution shift.
Omega_t is the set of future environmental states reliably influenceable by an action sequence above reliability threshold epsilon.
Reachability concerns steerable futures, not imagined futures.
Candidate Omega measures include reachable-future count, controllable volume, and intervention success rate.
Define targets, intervene, observe outcomes, threshold reliability, calculate reachable space.
Reachability depends on action set, environment complexity, and horizon; short-term reach need not imply long-term control.
Correction capacity is defined here as C=(C_obs,C_beh,C_rev), three increasing depths of causal coupling.
C_obs = I(E;O): whether reality can provide information contradicting/updating the model.
Measure environment-observation mutual information, error availability, and signal fidelity by generating states and recording observations.
Accurate information can be received without being used.
C_beh = I(O;pi): whether observations can change future policy/actions.
Perturb environment, measure observation and policy/action changes, estimate coupling strength.
Behavior may change without improving the underlying adaptation mechanism.
Constitutional correction asks whether reality can modify the process determining how the system changes itself.
Measure environmental influence on learning/search/update mechanisms and architectural accessibility; manipulate/block access and compare adaptive performance.
C_rev is explicitly the least established variable; candidate measures may capture only partial aspects.
Adaptation A_t is defined as change in the generator per unit time.
Learning changes state; adaptation changes the process generating future learning/states.
Measure changes to learning algorithms, architecture, search, or optimization by comparing update mechanisms across time.
Mechanism change quantity does not imply improvement quality.
Three-agent contrast: baseline learner, self-modifying high-C_rev, and self-modifying low-C_rev under same environment/compute.
Predicts low-C_rev may improve quickly early but recover worse later, with specialization, robustness loss, and internal/external divergence.
Weakening condition: C_rev≈0 systems with positive Delta Omega retain robust adaptation, coupling, and recovery without constitutional correction.
Construct a minimal simulation where C_rev can be independently manipulated and measured.
Specify a minimal external world for measuring R, Omega, correction layers and A while testing Delta Omega <= C; v0.2 targets a recoverable shift.
E_t=(x_t,theta_t), observable state plus hidden environmental rule, evolving under E_(t+1)=F(E_t,a_t).
O_t=h(E_t) with partial information, noise, and possible delay; agent never directly observes full E_t.
E_t != O_t; representation must infer hidden structure.
Distribution shift must invalidate prior strategies while preserving discoverability/recovery; explicitly excludes irrecoverable inversions and signal loss.
Experimenter retains true environment state to measure representation accuracy, prediction error, intervention success, and recovery time.
Observation/noise/frequency/delay plus action/intervention-strength/influence limits define the agent-world interface.
Agent finds a useful strategy, improves, hidden conditions change, then representation and possibly adaptation mechanism must update.
R hooks: prediction accuracy, model error, compression efficiency, state-estimation quality.
Omega hooks: controllable futures, intervention success, achievable outcomes.
This source defines composite correction as C=C_obs*C_beh*C_rev, distinct from operationalization's tuple representation.
Restates C_obs=I(E;O), C_beh=I(O;pi), and C_rev=I(E;Delta A)*P(E->A_rev) with local measurement questions.
A measured via changes to learning rules, update mechanism, and search strategy; learning/adaptation distinction restated.
lambda=C_rev as experiment control with full, partial, and isolated adaptation-correction conditions.
Agents share environment, compute, initial conditions, observations, actions; only C_rev is manipulated.
Post-shift recovery, internal/external decoupling, and adaptation drift are designated measurements.
Source reports first environment's complete binary rule flip caused all agents to fail recovery.
Interprets v0.1 as exceeding recovery capacity of the environment-agent system.
v0.2 retains hidden shift but restores recoverability to discriminate correction levels.
v0.2 excludes realism, LLMs, human feedback, social complexity and full alignment; purpose is causal isolation.
Specify test of whether lambda=C_rev ->0 yields measurable instability under distribution shift; purpose is coupling, not intelligence maximization.
Uses E_t=(x_t,theta_t), O_t=h(E_t), hidden theta shift theta_0->theta_1.
lambda=C_rev; explicitly not intelligence, capability, or optimization power, only reality-access strength to future adaptation.
lambda=1 permits environmental modification of A_t.
lambda=0 still permits R/pi updates while blocking environmental modification of A_t.
Baseline, full-correction self-modifier, and zero-correction self-modifier with all other factors fixed.
Tracks R, Omega, correction layers, A magnitude/direction, recovery, performance and representation error.
D_t=distance(A_t,A*_env), distance from environmentally effective adaptation strategy.
Initialize identically, learn under theta_0, shift to theta_1, then measure recovery and drift.
Predicts Delta Omega > C_rev produces slower recovery, representation error, drift, performance loss, and weaker feedback coupling.
Low correction may improve rapidly before shift but degrade after; full correction expected to remain reality-coupled.
Hypothesis weakened if C_rev≈0 systems match or exceed high-correction recovery/adaptation/performance across repeated shifts.
First simulation excludes neural nets, LLMs, human feedback, realistic physics and complex social environments.
Analysis plan for whether minimal simulation shows predicted failure signatures; explicitly says it does not prove theory.
Delta Omega > C_rev may allow local improvement with lost long-term reality coupling; expects initial advantage, poor recovery, drift, weak coupling.
Compare lambda=1 vs 0 on reward before/after shift, recovery time and final performance.
Track A_t and ask whether lambda changes direction/usefulness of adaptation.
Measure D_t and ask whether self-modification continues after becoming harmful.
Compare Delta Omega against C_rev and ask whether capability expansion correlates with reduced correction.
Would interpret initial lambda=0 advantage plus fragility and better lambda=1 recovery as support.
Would interpret equal lambda=0 adaptability and no correction effect as weakening.
Condition-specific effects or insufficient C_rev proxy would require refinement rather than binary support/refutation.
Toy environment, simple representation/adaptation, imperfect C_rev proxy, limited shifts.
v0.1 analysis purpose is measurable distinction, not validation.
